newsitem.title: UK: Britain's supermarkets cautious on modified soy.
newsitem.headline: Britain's supermarkets cautious on modified soy.

text.p: Major UK supermarket chains acknowledge consumer concerns over genetically modified products and are insisting on rigorous scrutiny to ensure they pose no hazard before approval is given for their sale, industry sources said.
Supermarkets plan to give customers as much information as they can, with some publishing lists of products free from soy.
Modified U.S. soybeans, due to arrive in Europe in November, cannot yet be segregated from non-genetically altered material.
Retailer hoped this would be possible by the end of the next growing season.

Retailers say genetically modified foods have been approved by regulatory bodies and they welcome the European Union Novel Foods Regulation, which they say will harmonise labelling requirements for such foods throughout the EU.
